findings.claim: The bounded current related-function surface contains 75 functions, including 10 cached, 4 context, 1 manifest and 4 receipt-named functions.
Whitespace-normalized body comparison finds 2 duplicate-body groups containing 5 functions; duplication alone does not establish defect or safe deletion.

Existing manifest/receipt functions have mixed volatility and EXECUTE grants; notably release_bundle_manifest_v1 is STABLE and executable, while several receipt functions are VOLATILE. No function was invoked.
track_functions is none and pg_stat_user_functions exposes zero rows/calls for the bounded family, so zero stats cannot be interpreted as zero runtime use.
Frozen P0 declares 38 callers and 76 callee edges, with max declared out-degree 5 and no zero-callee caller; this is a static declared graph, not runtime telemetry.

assumptions.text: Existing cache/context/manifest/receipt surfaces may satisfy evidence needs and should be evaluated before inventing a new subsystem.
Exact/normalized body duplication may represent intentional compatibility variants.
VOLATILE functions may write or have side effects; EXECUTE privilege alone is not permission to invoke them during read-only research.
track_functions=none makes zero function stats non-informative about usage.
Static declared edges are not equivalent to runtime call frequency or criticality.

justifications.claim: Duplicate-body cleanup is not currently justified
